name: Pyth BTC/USD price momentum
description: Momentum of the Pyth Network BTC/USD aggregate price on the oracle lane, from the Hermes stream source pyth.hermes.btc-usd.price. Pyth publishes at roughly one hertz, so this identity samples the aggregate price one-second causal. return_bps_1s, return_bps_10s, return_bps_30s, return_bps_1m, return_bps_5m, and return_bps_15m are simple basis-point returns of the newest aggregate price against the price one, ten, thirty, sixty, three-hundred, and nine-hundred seconds back on the causal ring. direction_5m is down, flat, or up from the full-precision five-minute return, with flat exactly zero. Any missing or stale one-second observation breaks continuity and restarts the fifteen-minute warm-up; the identity is ready only once the ring holds the fifteen-minute window of contiguous samples. This definition ships approved but refuse-closed today, on the same precedent as btc.pyth.oracle_reference: no processor consumes pyth.hermes.btc-usd.price on the oracle lane yet, so the identity publishes no ready values and refuses at start-up. It begins publishing once the Pyth Hermes stream is wired as a lane input (slice C4). Reads only Pyth and predicts nothing. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
